Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a distal radius fracture consistent with the mechanism of
injury described. Over the course of 24 visits, care followed a typical progression: immobilization, reduction and casting,
followed by structured physical therapy focused on range of motion and grip strength. Visit frequency decreased steadily as
healing progressed and symptoms improved. Examination findings included localized tenderness and reduced grip strength over
the fracture site, which correlate with the imaging results, while neurovascular testing and sensation remained within normal
limits. No prior injury or treatment to the affected wrist was reported or found in available records. Billing reflects the planned
care, with no duplicate or repeated charges identified. At the most recent visit, the patient had regained most of the functional
motion expected at this stage of recovery and was discharged to a home exercise program with instructions to return if symptoms
worsen.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.

- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
